Get started with zutable

Source: vignettes/zutable.Rmd
zutable.Rmd
library(zutable)

A data.frame does not know its types: a column can change from integer to character with one assignment, and an error surfaces only when the data reaches the code that breaks. A zutable always knows its schema, and every query is checked against it before any data is read. This page uses one small table of trades throughout.

trades <- zutable(
  id       = c(1L, 1L, 2L, 2L, 3L),
  day      = as.Date("2026-01-01") + 0:4,
  px       = c(10.5, 11, 20, 19.5, 7),
  qty      = c(100L, 50L, 10L, 30L, 200L),
  notional = NA_real_
)
schema(trades)
#> <zutable_schema> 5 fields
#>   id int32
#>   day date
#>   px float64
#>   qty int32
#>   notional float64

Query with SQL’s clauses

The bracket takes SQL’s clauses as named arguments over bare column names, and runs them in SQL’s logical order whatever order they are written in.

# Open: `.()` against another spelling inside `select` (ergonomics tests)
trades[where  = day >= "2026-01-02",
       select = .(vwap = sum(px * qty) / sum(qty), n = count()),
       by     = id,
       order  = desc(vwap)]
#> <zutable> 3 rows x 3 columns
#>   id      vwap      n
#>   <int32> <float64> <not_null(int32)>
#> 1 2       19.625    2
#> 2 1       11.000    1
#> 3 3       7.000     1

Schemas are known before data is

Every function comes from a closed, typed vocabulary, so the result’s schema follows from the input’s. A value that would change a column’s type is an error, not a silent conversion.

schema(trades[select = .(.all, value = px * qty)])
#> <zutable_schema> 6 fields
#>   id int32
#>   day date
#>   px float64
#>   qty int32
#>   notional float64
#>   value float64
trades[, { qty := px * 2 }]   # zutable_schema_error: qty is int32
#> Error in `[.zutable`:
#> ! column `qty` is int32; the update would make it float64

Update in place, then freeze

:= writes into existing columns in place, and never adds one. A block is checked as a whole and committed at once. freeze() marks where a table’s values are final.

trades[, {
  notional := px * qty
}]
#> <zutable> 5 rows x 5 columns
#>   id      day        px        qty     notional
#>   <int32> <date>     <float64> <int32> <float64>
#> 1 1       2026-01-01 10.5      100     1050
#> 2 1       2026-01-02 11.0      50      550
#> 3 2       2026-01-03 20.0      10      200
#> 4 2       2026-01-04 19.5      30      585
#> 5 3       2026-01-05 7.0       200     1400
freeze(trades)
trades
#> <zutable> 5 rows x 5 columns, frozen
#>   id      day        px        qty     notional
#>   <int32> <date>     <float64> <int32> <float64>
#> 1 1       2026-01-01 10.5      100     1050
#> 2 1       2026-01-02 11.0      50      550
#> 3 2       2026-01-03 20.0      10      200
#> 4 2       2026-01-04 19.5      30      585
#> 5 3       2026-01-05 7.0       200     1400

One plan, several engines

A lazy table records steps instead of running them. explain() shows the plan with each step’s schema, and collect() runs it locally or as SQL.

r <- lazy(trades)[select = .(n = count()), by = id]
explain(r)
collect(r)
collect(r, engine = "duckdb")
